title: Structural basis of antagonizing the vitamin K catalytic cycle for anticoagulation
authors: Liu S, Li S, Shen G, Sukumar N, Krezel AM, Li W

result: Eleven crystal structures of human vitamin K epoxide reductase (VKOR) and a VKOR-like paralog with substrates and antagonists. VKOR is an endoplasmic reticulum membrane enzyme; the cycle begins with epoxidation of vitamin K hydroquinone, which drives gamma-carboxylation of coagulation factors, and VKOR reduces the epoxide first to the quinone and then to the hydroquinone, each step coupled to oxidation of two active-site cysteines. Vitamin K antagonists, including warfarin, inhibit VKOR at both the epoxide and the quinone reduction steps.
